content.title: Brazil's Gol Airlines secures new financing to support Chapter 11 exit
content.summary: Brazilian airline Gol on Thursday announced that it has struck a new deal with key creditors, paving the way for the company to emerge from Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection likely by the end of June.  With the new development, Gol has now secured at least $1.375 billion in financing to exit bankruptcy, the filing showed.  Gol said that support from this majority group of creditors will substantially increase the chances of its restructuring plan being approved.

content.title: GOL Linhas Aéreas Files Chapter 11 Reorganization Plan
content.summary: GOL Linhas Aereas Inteligentes SA (GOLLQ) has released an update. content.title: Brazil aid to airlines on the way, says airports minister
content.summary: A Brazilian government-backed credit line for struggling airlines should be ready by early 2025, helping the industry ride out a bumpy stretch for big carriers, Ports and Airports Minister Silvio Costa Filho told Reuters.  Gol Linhas Aereas, which is negotiating its exit from bankruptcy protection, and Azul, which recently renegotiated debts to raise fresh capital, are both in talks with the government about the credit, Costa Filho said.  Azul confirmed it is in talks with the government about the credit line.
